meta.title: Garlic Butter Pasta
meta.textType: the main topic of a text

paragraphs: Garlic Butter Pasta, posted by May. On Saturday, the Explorers learned to cook pasta with Chef Lucy. I ask the questions for the club, so I had a job. I held a microphone and made a record of Chef Lucy for the blog. She spoke about four things, and I wrote them in four parts. I hope that you will cook it at home.

First, the smell. The smell of garlic is very strong. But a whole garlic does not smell much. It smells strong only when someone cuts it. When garlic is in hot butter, the smell fills the whole kitchen. Chef Lucy said, "Your nose tells you when the garlic is ready." "It smells like a restaurant!" said Mia. We all smiled, because the smell was lovely.

Second, the butter sauce. The sauce has only three things: butter, garlic, and a little oil. First, melt the butter in a small pan. Then add the garlic. Do not make the pan too hot, because garlic burns fast. Cook it for one minute, but do not make it brown. Chef Lucy showed us a soft, golden sauce.

Third, the boiling. You boil the pasta in a big pot of water. Use a lot of water, so the pasta can move. The water must be very hot. We stood far from the pot, because it was dangerous. Put in the pasta, and wait for ten minutes. Take one piece out and try it. It must be soft, but not too soft.

Last, the seasoning. We put the pasta into the sauce and mixed it with a big spoon. Then we season it with salt and a little black pepper. Chef Lucy said, "Season the food slowly, and try it again." "Too much salt is not good," she said. Everybody had a plate, and we ate at one long table. Chef Lucy gave each of us a little garlic to take home. Mia liked it, and Leo asked for more. At home, I listened to my record of Chef Lucy again. Which part do you like best?
